quest.title: Crash Course on Inazuman Fashion
quest.description: Ogura Mio, the owner of Ogura Textiles & Kimonos, is rather anxious about something...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: This is no way to continue doing business...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm sorry. I was just a little lost in my own thoughts. Are you here to buy some clothes?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: The high-class silks from Liyue remain out of stock, but we still have the latest kimonos.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You used to import material from Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Yes. Before, we were often able to secure high-end silk from Liyue such as those that the Feiyun Commerce Guild makes from Silk Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: But with the current situation here, we haven't been able to import that sort of silk in a while now. We've been having to rely on our existing stock to continue operations.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Every bolt of silk we use here is one we're not getting back...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I originally planned to design some novel kimono patterns myself, or use some new dyes to make new cloth and attract customers.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: But I can't think of anything that might be considered a "novel" pattern...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Traveler, you've seen a lot, I'm sure. Have you encountered any designs that you might consider "novel"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't say so, exactly...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. Um, this might be rather presumptuous of me, but... could you help me ask other outlanders about patterns that we could use?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: I'm the only one running Ogura Textiles & Kimonos at the moment, so I can't leave the store. If I want to gather information, I can only ask others to do it for me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Great, let me think... You should go ask Miss Tang Wen and Mr. Ramsay. Perhaps they will have some new ideas.

talks.objective: Ask Tang Wen about the kimonos

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, do you have any ideas for kimono patterns?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Kimono patterns? I'm afraid I don't know anything about that...

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: But if you were to ask me... I think that books might look great as a design on a kimono.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Hmm, books printed on kimonos... Now wouldn't that be interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, do you have any ideas for kimono patterns?

dialogues.speaker: Ramsay
dialogues.text: Kimono patterns? Haha, I'm not exactly an expert on that.

dialogues.speaker: Ramsay
dialogues.text: But if I were to choose a design, I'd go with tea sets. Those would look neat on a kimono.

dialogues.speaker: Ramsay
dialogues.text: A kimono printed with a tea set design... Hahaha, now that certainly would have an Inazuman feel.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: So did you ask them about it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I did.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Great! So what did they say?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Books and... tea sets? That sounds interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: But how should we make them exactly? Hmm, I need to give this a bit more thought...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Thank you, Traveler. This information has proved extremely useful to me. Please, accept these as a token of my appreciation.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Mio
dialogues.text: Perhaps Miss Tang Wen and Mr. Ramsay will have some new ideas...
